// Platform legal

Blindsight third-party licences

Applies to the on-device names model versions 4 and 4-fp16 · Updated 19 November 2026

blindsight.io/platform/legal/third-party

This document covers the Blindsight platform (the console, the desktop apps and the APIs). The blindsight.io website has its own privacy policy.

1. What this page lists

The models, tokenizer and datasets behind the on-device names model, with their creators, licences, sources and the changes Blindsight made. The model files are downloaded by the desktop app after installation. The weights and the tokenizer file are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0; the base model and the datasets keep the licences named below. The libraries and programs inside the installers are listed in the licence notices supplied with the software.

Blindsight also generated sentences by script from its own templates and lists, and had a language model write synthetic sentences with the names filled in by script. These are Blindsight's own material. No data from any Blindsight customer was used.

3. Full notice shipped with the model files

This is the notice that comes with the INT8 model files, followed by the one change that differs in the FP16 files. It includes the Apache License 2.0 text for the base model.

The Blindsight on-device names model

This model detects person names, organisations, places and dates in text on the
device. It was trained by Blindsight from the base model below on the datasets
below. The model weights and the tokenizer file in this directory are licensed
under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International licence
(CC BY-SA 4.0): https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode

Base model
  distilbert-base-multilingual-cased, Apache License 2.0
  https://huggingface.co/distilbert/distilbert-base-multilingual-cased
  Sanh et al., DistilBERT, 2019. The Apache-2.0 notice of the base model is
  preserved here, and the full text of the Apache License 2.0 is reproduced at
  the end of this file. The base model was modified: its weights were
  fine-tuned by Blindsight for token classification (names, organisations,
  places and dates) and the result was converted to ONNX, with reduced numeric
  precision (FP16 or INT8) in some variants.

Training data and attribution
  Universal NER v1 (CC BY-SA 4.0). Mayhew et al., Universal NER: A Gold-Standard
  Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Benchmark, NAACL 2024.
  https://www.universalner.org
  Treebanks used: English-EWT, Portuguese-Bosque, Chinese-GSD and
  Chinese-GSDSimp (Universal Dependencies treebanks, CC BY-SA 4.0, with the
  Universal NER annotations).
  Europeana Newspapers NER corpora (CC0). Europeana Newspapers Project,
  2012-2015. https://github.com/EuropeanaNewspapers/ner-corpora
  ANERcorp, CAMeL Lab train/test splits (CC BY-SA 4.0). Benajiba, Rosso and
  Benedi Ruiz, 2007; Obeid et al., CAMeL Tools, LREC 2020.
  https://camel.abudhabi.nyu.edu/anercorp/
  AQMAR Arabic Wikipedia Named Entity Corpus (CC BY-SA 3.0). Mohit, Schneider,
  Bhowmick, Oflazer and Smith, Recall-Oriented Learning of Named Entities in
  Arabic Wikipedia, EACL 2012. https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~ark/ArabicNER/
  CC BY-SA 3.0 section 4(b) permits an adaptation to be distributed under a
  later version of the licence with the same licence elements, here CC BY-SA
  4.0.
  GermEval 2014 NER shared task data (CC BY 4.0). Benikova, Biemann, Reznicek,
  2014. https://sites.google.com/site/germeval2014ner/
  WikiNER and wikigold (CC BY 4.0). Nothman, Ringland, Radford, Murphy, Curran,
  Learning multilingual named entity recognition from Wikipedia, Artificial
  Intelligence 2013; Balasuriya et al., 2009.
  https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.5462500
  MultiCoNER v2 (CC BY 4.0). Fetahu, Chen, Kar, Rokhlenko, Malmasi, 2023.
  https://multiconer.github.io
  LUMII AiLab FullStack, Latvian named entities (CC BY-SA 4.0).
  https://github.com/LUMII-AILab/FullStack
  Wikidata name labels (CC0), used to fill synthetic sentences.
  https://www.wikidata.org
  Several of the corpora above (AQMAR, GermEval 2014, WikiNER, wikigold and
  MultiCoNER v2) consist of sentences from Wikipedia, which is licensed under
  CC BY-SA.
  Round 6 adds sentences generated by Blindsight scripts from its own
  templates, and same-type name swaps inside the corpora above, filled with
  the Wikidata labels above. Round 8 adds sentences generated by Blindsight
  scripts from its own templates (JSON, YAML, tables, logs, e-mail headers,
  citations, chat exports, tool calls and short questions that contain names),
  filled with Wikidata name labels and corpus name frequencies from the
  corpora above. Round 9 adds sentences generated by Blindsight scripts from its
  own templates (multi-record logs, CSV cells, user= lines, mail headers,
  headings, usernames and bot names kept as non-names, organisation classes,
  first names with surnames that are also common nouns), and same-type
  organisation swaps inside the real training sentences of the corpora above
  (German, English, Arabic, French). No new third-party data.
  Synthetic sentences written with a language model, with names,
  organisations, places and dates filled in by script, so every label is
  exact.
  Further sentences (government bodies, product and tool names, questions)
  generated by script from lists written by Blindsight, and real training
  sentences of the corpora above with organisations swapped by script.
  Round 11 adds, by script from lists written by Blindsight, organisation
  names of companies, newspapers and magazines, venues and clubs, universities
  and schools, parties and international bodies in German and Portuguese
  sentences (templates, and real training sentences of the corpora above with
  an organisation swapped), further German, Austrian and Swiss business and
  public-body names, persons with fresh first names and surnames in many
  frames, and further non-name examples. No new third-party data.
  Round 12 adds, by script from lists written by Blindsight and the Wikidata
  name labels above: person names in English, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch,
  French and Portuguese (first names after labels and in signatures, surnames,
  initials, public figures, placeholder names, titled and fictional names, and
  common words kept as non-names); organisation names (public bodies and
  agencies, armed forces and social-security bodies, department and team nouns,
  sports leagues, clubs and venues, newspapers and journals, universities,
  schools, libraries and museums, small companies with legal forms, all-capital
  company names, company names in code, configuration and e-mail text); further
  German, Austrian and Swiss organisation classes; and further non-name
  examples. No new third-party data.
  Round 13 adds, by script from lists written by Blindsight and the Wikidata
  name labels above: person names in English, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch,
  French and Portuguese (lone first names after verbs of address and in
  sign-offs, surnames without a title, initial forms, public figures and
  stage names in ordinary questions, placeholder names in templates, titled
  names, and capitalised common words, role words, assistant and tool names
  kept as non-names), and replays, unchanged, person-bearing training
  sentences of the corpora above (including ANERcorp, AQMAR, GermEval 2014,
  Europeana, WikiNER, MultiCoNER v2 and Universal NER) that were also used in
  earlier rounds. No new third-party data. Round 13 also adds, by script from
  lists written by Blindsight, non-name examples (occupation words that are
  also surnames, plural colour nouns, postcodes with city names). No new
  third-party data.

These datasets were converted to a token-classification format and relabelled
to person, organisation, place and date; entity classes were mapped; some
sentences were case-changed or had names swapped.

Provided as is without warranties, as set out in the disclaimer of warranties
of the licences named above.

Based on distilbert-base-multilingual-cased (Apache-2.0), fine-tuned by
Blindsight Technologies AG.

Modification statement (this variant: dynamic per-channel INT8)
  model.onnx in this directory was converted to ONNX and INT8 quantised by
  Blindsight Technologies AG from the weights, which Blindsight
  Technologies AG fine-tuned from distilbert-base-multilingual-cased
  (https://huggingface.co/distilbert/distilbert-base-multilingual-cased).
  tokenizer.json is the tokenizer of that base model.

Organisation list
  Organisation names are taken from Wikidata (CC0); names belong to their
  owners. The file orgs-v1.json holds labels and identifiers only, no
  Wikipedia text (see NOTICE-orgs-v1.txt). It is a separate file, not
  covered by the CC BY-SA 4.0 grant above, and the "license" field of
  manifest.json does not apply to it.

Integrity checks are not access restrictions
  The model files are shipped as separate, unencrypted files. Code signing
  and the sha256 values in manifest.json only let the Blindsight app check
  that the files are intact; they do not restrict copying, modifying or
  sharing these files under their licences.

No data from any Blindsight customer was used.
